title: The Human Body: Parts and Organs

questions.stem: Which organ takes in air when you breathe?
questions.explanation: The lungs take in air. The heart pumps blood, the liver cleans blood, and the stomach mashes up food.

questions.stem: Look at the picture of the body. Which number shows the knee?
questions.image_alt: Outline of a child with body parts numbered 1 to 11.
questions.explanation: Number 10 is the knee. It is a joint in the middle of the leg, so your leg can bend there.

questions.stem: Look at the picture of the body. Which number shows the elbow?
questions.image_alt: Outline of a child with body parts numbered 1 to 11.
questions.explanation: Number 5 is the elbow. It is the joint in the middle of the arm that lets you bend your arm.

questions.stem: Look at the skeleton. Which number shows the bone that protects the brain?
questions.image_alt: A human skeleton with some bones numbered.
questions.explanation: Number 1 is the skull. It is a hard bone shell around the brain. The ribs (2) protect the heart and lungs.

questions.stem: Look at the skeleton. Which number shows the bones that make a cage to protect the heart and lungs?
questions.image_alt: A human skeleton with some bones numbered.
questions.explanation: Number 2 is the ribs. They curve around the chest like a cage and protect the heart and lungs.

questions.stem: Look at the arm. Which number shows the joint, where two bones meet and bend?
questions.image_alt: An arm with a bone, two muscles and the elbow joint numbered 1 to 4.
questions.explanation: Number 4 is the elbow joint. A joint is where two bones meet, and it lets the arm bend.

questions.stem: Joints are where two bones meet and bend. Look at the body. Which numbers show joints? Choose all that are right.
questions.image_alt: Outline of a child with body parts numbered 1 to 11.
questions.explanation: The elbow (5) and the knee (10) are joints that bend. The head (1), chest (7) and foot (11) are not joints.

questions.stem: Match each picture to its job.
pairs: holds you up and gives you shape
questions.explanation: The brain controls the body and helps you think. The heart pumps blood. The lungs take in air. Bones hold you up and give you your shape.

questions.stem: Match each organ to its job.
pairs: take goodness from food into your blood
controls your body and helps you think
questions.explanation: The stomach mashes food. The intestines take goodness from food into the blood. The liver cleans blood, the bladder stores urine, and the brain is the controller.

questions.stem: The ___ is the bone that protects your brain.
questions.explanation: The skull is a hard shell of bone around the brain. It protects the brain from bumps.

questions.stem: Muscles are joined to bones. When a muscle pulls, the bone moves.
questions.explanation: Muscles pull on bones to make them move. Bones and muscles work together so we can walk, run and kick.

questions.stem: Your heart only beats when you are awake.
questions.explanation: Your heart beats all day and all night, about 100 times every minute, even when you are asleep.

questions.stem: Which of these are organs inside your body? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: The heart, lungs and stomach are organs inside the body. The knee and the hand are outside parts of the body.

questions.stem: Sort these body parts. Are they on the outside of the body or are they organs inside?
questions.explanation: We can see the head, arms, knees and feet on the outside. The brain, heart, lungs, stomach and kidneys are organs inside the body.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to count your heartbeat for one minute.
sequence: Sit quietly and find the pulse on your wrist.
Write the number of beats in 1 minute.
questions.explanation: Find your pulse, count the beats for 15 seconds, multiply by 4 (because 15 seconds is a quarter of a minute), then write the answer.

questions.stem: How do your bones and muscles help you kick a ball?
questions.model_answer: The muscles in my leg pull on the leg bones, so my leg moves and kicks the ball.
questions.explanation: Muscles are joined to bones. When the leg muscles pull on the leg bones, the leg swings and kicks the ball.

questions.stem: Why do you breathe faster when you run?
questions.explanation: When you run, your body needs more air. Your lungs work harder and take in air faster.

questions.stem: Rafi counted 33 heartbeats in 15 seconds after jumping. In 1 minute his heart beats ___ times.
questions.explanation: One minute is four lots of 15 seconds, so 33 × 4 = 132 beats in a minute.

questions.stem: Joy rides his bicycle to school in Dhaka. Why should he wear a helmet?
options: It makes his heart beat slower.
It protects his skull and brain if he falls.
questions.explanation: The skull protects the brain, but a hard bump can still hurt it. A helmet gives extra protection if he falls.

questions.stem: After a race, Anika's heart beats very fast. Her friend says, 'That is normal. Her muscles needed more blood while she ran.' Is her friend right?
questions.explanation: When you exercise, your muscles work hard and need more blood. Your heart pumps faster to bring it.

questions.stem: The doctor tells Nadia she has grown 5 cm this year. She was 115 cm tall last year. How tall is she now?
questions.explanation: Add the growth to last year's height: 115 + 5 = 120 cm.

questions.stem: The doctor says Nadia's heart is strong and her lungs are clear. Which of these help keep a body healthy? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Healthy food, outdoor play and clean drinking water all help the body. Sitting still all day does not help muscles, bones or the heart.

questions.stem: Mina counted her heartbeats for one minute (example data): sitting 80, walking 100, running 140. How many more times did her heart beat in a minute when she was running than when she was sitting?
questions.explanation: Subtract: 140 − 80 = 60. Her heart beat 60 more times a minute when running.

questions.stem: Mina's heart beat 80 times a minute when sitting and 140 times a minute when running. Explain why her heart beats faster when she runs.
questions.model_answer: When she runs, her muscles work hard and need more blood, so her heart pumps faster.
questions.explanation: Running makes the muscles work hard. They need more blood, so the heart pumps faster to send it.

questions.stem: Bones are hard and cannot bend. So how can you bend your arm at the elbow?
options: Your arm bones are soft like rubber.
Muscles pull on the bones where they meet at the elbow joint.
questions.explanation: A joint is where two bones meet. Muscles are joined to bones, and when a muscle pulls, the bones move at the joint.

questions.stem: The kidneys make urine (wee), and the ___ stores it.
questions.explanation: The kidneys clean the blood and make urine. The bladder stores urine until you go to the toilet.
